name: Film noir
summary: A black and white crime film lit from one hard source. Venetian-blind bars, rain and smoke cut the frame. The camera sits low and tilts. A tired man tells the story in voice-over and the plot closes on him.

philosophy.core_thesis: One hard lamp, a low camera and a narrow strip of light turn a city into a trap, so the viewer feels the fate of the hero before the hero does.
design_principles: Light the set with 1 hard key and no fill, and let 40% to 60% of the frame fall to black.
Shoot in black and white at 1.37:1 with a 25mm to 35mm lens and deep focus on 3 planes.
Put the camera 0.5 to 1.0 m low, and tilt it 5° to 15° off the level for a tense scene.
Throw bars, rain and smoke shadows across a face with a gobo or a slatted blind.
Cut at an average shot length of 6 to 10 s and use a long take for a talk in a car or a room.
Tell the story through a voice-over by the hero, and let it run at 5% to 15% of the runtime.
Set the scene at night in a city, in a bar, a flat or an office with a lit sign outside.
anti_patterns: A bright happy ending with a kiss
Soft diffusion on the heroine's face

composition.framing: A 1.37:1 frame cut into bands by shadow; a face lit in a strip across the eyes, a body half in the dark and a doorway or a stair as a second frame.
composition.staging_in_depth: 3 planes in deep focus: a foreground edge or lamp, the actor, and a lit window or door at the back.
composition.subject_placement: Off the centre by 1/3, with 2:1 more empty dark space in front of the look than behind.

principles.rule: Let a single hard key throw a bright strip against a black mass.
Light with one hard key and leave the fill out.
Cut the frame with a blind, a door or a stair so that a second frame sits inside the first.
principles.value: 1 inner frame, 10% to 30% of the view

principles.rule: Place the camera low and tilt it for a scene of threat.
Cut at a steady pace, and hold one long take for a talk in a car or a room.

camera_and_movement.movement: A slow dolly or crane that follows the hero and stops at a door; a low static shot for a talk; a rare handheld run.
camera_and_movement.support: Dolly, crane and a low tripod

lens_and_format.focal_length: 25mm to 35mm (35mm format), wide with deep focus
lens_and_format.aperture: f/8 to f/16 for deep focus
lens_and_format.resolution: 35mm black and white negative; scan at 2K or 4K
equipment: a hard Fresnel lamp with a gobo

light.quality: Hard and directional with sharp shadow edges; smoke makes the beam visible.
light.direction: From the side or from above and behind, at 45° to 90° to the lens axis.
light.source: Hard key lamp, a lit window blind and a street sign

colour_and_grade.treatment: Rich black and white with a full grey scale, deep blacks and a clipped bright strip.
grade_recipe: Convert to black and white and set the black point at 2% and the white point at 98%.
Use a contrast curve of +30% and crush the shadows below 5%.
Add a vignette of 10% to 15% on the frame edge.
Do not add a tint or a colour accent.
colour_and_grade.texture: Fine 35mm grain at 15% to 20%, with a smoke haze in the beam

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 6 to 10 s (estimate; check Cinemetrics for each title)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 1 s for an insert of a gun or a clock to 3 min for a long talk
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Cut on a look or a line and match the eyeline; hold a long take when the hero is trapped in a room.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Hard cut, a dissolve at a time jump and a fade to black at the end of a reel.

sound.approach: Studio sound with a close voice; a hard room tone, steps on a wet street and a distant siren.
sound.dialogue: Fast, dry and cynical, with a voice-over by the hero.
sound.music: A brass and strings score that holds 2 to 3 motifs; a jazz club cue in the bar scene.
sound.loudness: −24 LUFS integrated, narrow dynamic range for the original mix

titles_and_graphics.treatment: A hard title card in white on black over a shadow of the city; the credits on a rolling or a held card.
titles_and_graphics.type: A condensed sans-serif or a bold upright in white upper case, 3 to 5 s per card.

shot_primer.opening: Open at night on a wet street or a lit window, then cut to a face in a strip of shadow within 8 s.

shot_list.shot: Hero in a doorway, 3 planes deep
Gun in a hand under a lamp

positive: venetian blind shadows on a face
cigarette smoke in a light beam

emotion.target_response: Dread and fatalism: the viewer sees a trap close and knows that the hero cannot leave it.

use_cases: music video in black and white
avoid_when: The brief needs a warm, friendly or optimistic tone.
The scene needs even light for a product or a demo.

modifiers.how: Keep the night city and the hard key; add a saturated coloured source in cyan and magenta and shoot in colour.
Keep the black and white; move the camera into a real street with available light and non-professional actors.

sources.title: Paul Schrader, Notes on Film Noir (Film Comment, 1972)
Alain Silver and Elizabeth Ward, Film Noir: An Encyclopedic Reference to the American Style (Overlook Press, 3rd ed., 1992)
